message.content:
Here’s a mix of classic, modern, and cult‑favorite horror films you might enjoy:

| # | Title | Year | Director | Why it’s worth watching |
|---|-------|------|----------|------------------------|
| 1 | **The Shining** | 1980 | Stanley Kubrick | A masterclass in psychological terror and atmosphere. |
| 2 | **Hereditary** | 2018 | Ari Aster | A chilling family drama that turns into a supernatural nightmare. |
| 3 | **Get Out** | 2017 | Jordan Peele | Horror meets sharp social commentary. |
| 4 | **A Quiet Place** | 2018 | John Krasinski | Silence is the key to survival—thrilling and tense. |
| 5 | **Midsommar** | 2019 | Ari Aster | Daylight horror that’s as unsettling as it is beautiful. |
| 6 | **It Follows** | 2014 | David Robert Mitchell | A unique premise that keeps you on edge. |
| 7 | **The Conjuring** | 2013 | James Wan | A modern classic of haunted house scares. |
| 8 | **The Babadook** | 2014 | Jennifer Kent | Psychological horror with a hauntingly memorable monster. |
| 9 | **The Witch** | 2015 | Robert Eggers | Creepy, slow‑burning dread set in Puritan New England. |
|10 | **Suspiria (1977)** | 1977 | Dario Argento | A visually striking, gory classic of Italian giallo. |
|11 | **The Ring** | 2002 | Gore Verbinski | A modern retelling of a Japanese horror legend. |
|12 | **Paranormal Activity** | 2007 | Oren Peli | Found‑footage realism that makes the supernatural feel real. |
|13 | **The Cabin in the Woods** | 2012 | Drew Goddard | A meta‑take on horror tropes that’s both funny and scary. |
|14 | **The Others** | 2001 | Alejandro Amenábar | A moody, atmospheric ghost story with a twist. |
|15 | **The Exorcist** | 1973 | William Friedkin | The quintessential exorcism film that still terrifies. |

Feel free to pick based on your mood—whether you want a slow‑burn psychological thriller or a jump‑scare‑heavy slasher. Happy watching!
